clue.text: Wear for the female informer?

parts.note: a grass is British slang for a police informer
skirt is old slang for a woman

explanation.surface: A question about what a woman who tells tales to the police might put on.
explanation.walkthrough: The order is swapped: 'female informer' reads as one person, but the informer gives the first half and the female the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirt of grass is a garment, so it is something to wear.

clue.text: Bowl for the table

definitions.meaning: to bowl a ball or hoop along is to send it ...
a bread bun is set on the dinner table

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to send something trundling along, and a small loaf served at meals.

clue.text: Watch to the end, as the stand-in won't?

definitions.text: Watch to the end, as the stand-in won't?

parts.words: Watch to the end, as the stand-in won't?
parts.note: to stay to the finish of something; a stand-in, by contrast, is expected to get up and play, so does not stay on the bench

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to remain until something finishes, and also to stay out of the action, which a substitute must not do.

clue.text: Made fun of, bolted

definitions.meaning: jeered at or mocked
ate greedily and quickly

explanation.surface: Someone was mocked and then ran off.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both mocking someone and wolfing food down.

clue.text: Time to make something for the journalist

indicators.note: the letters of the word time are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A reporter is given time to produce a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is the anagram signal: the four letters of 'Time' are remade.
explanation.definitionFit: A news report or article is called an item in journalism.

clue.text: His little sister may reach to his waist or chest

definitions.text: His little sister may reach to his waist or chest

parts.words: His little sister may reach to his waist or chest
parts.note: reads as a lanky lad with a short sibling, but is a tall chest of drawers whose smaller companion, a lowboy, is waist high

explanation.surface: A small girl stands only as high as her big brother's middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'chest' is furniture: a tallboy is a tall chest of drawers, and the 'little sister' is a lower piece standing beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a high chest of drawers, as well as suggesting a tall lad.

clue.text: A kind of bird perch, might it be?

definitions.text: A kind of bird perch, might it be?

parts.words: A kind of bird perch, might it be?
parts.note: a perch is a fish, so a perch that acts like a bird would be an airborne fish

explanation.surface: A question about something a bird sits on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' tempts as a bird's resting place; it is the fish, and the 'bird' kind of fish is one that glides through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical sea creature glides above the water on wing-like fins, like a bird.

clue.text: One's to pour a drink out and be quick

indicators.note: pouring something out spills and scatters it, here the letters
completes the phrase pour out, signalling the rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter beyond the s
lime is a cordial or juice drink

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pour a drink and hurry up about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pour ... out' brackets the fodder: ONESTO plus LIME are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To act without delay is the idiom's meaning, the same as hurrying.

clue.text: He's well up in music

parts.note: seems to praise an expert musician, but describes a high male singing voice

explanation.surface: Praise for a man who knows a lot about music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well up' looks like 'knowledgeable'; it means pitched high.
explanation.definitionFit: This voice part sits high in the range, a male countertenor or high voice.

clue.text: How the doctor knows the malingerers for what they are?

definitions.text: How the doctor knows the malingerers for what they are?

parts.words: How the doctor knows the malingerers for what they are?
parts.note: the idiom means only too thoroughly, and literally the shirkers are perfectly healthy

explanation.surface: A doctor sees through patients faking illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means 'only too well' (knowing someone thoroughly), and the shammers really are well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means painfully thoroughly, and here also that the patients are entirely healthy.

clue.text: Get in touch with when I sail out East

indicators.note: letters sailing out are thrown out of order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Contacting someone at the moment one sets sail eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I SAIL to LIAIS, then E for East closes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To work in cooperation or keep contact with someone is to stay in touch.

clue.text: Marked "seen"

definitions.meaning: having marks or spots on it
noticed or caught sight of

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: dotted with marks, and noticed by someone.

clue.text: Sights that may be for your eyes only

definitions.meaning: impressive displays or shows

definitions.text: that may be for your eyes only
definitions.meaning: glasses are made to fit one wearer's eyes

explanation.surface: Secret things meant only for one viewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For your eyes only' recalls secret documents; glasses suit only their owner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means grand public shows as well as a pair of glasses.

clue.text: An air of "Just you wait!"

definitions.meaning: a famous aria from Puccini's Madama Butterfly
a promise that some day things will come about

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase titles a celebrated operatic aria and is a promise that things will happen eventually.

clue.text: Finally murmured foolishly some objection

indicators.note: foolish behaviour garbles the letters into a new order
only the closing part of the word murmured is used

explanation.surface: At last somebody mutters a silly protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' keeps the end of 'murmured', MURED, and 'foolishly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun this word means a hesitation or protest, an objection.

clue.text: Heading for, or on the point of so doing

definitions.meaning: travelling towards a place

definitions.text: on the point of so doing
definitions.meaning: about to do something

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means travelling towards somewhere and also being about to act.

clue.text: Bring back a dog to guard or a bunch of them

indicators.note: a down clue's pieces brought back read from the bottom upwards
the dog guards the small word by standing round it

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: Fetching a dog to guard either one or a whole pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring back' turns the whole container, so the little word ends up read as RO inside the reversed dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster or set of things or people is a bunch.

clue.text: Fine around the east, rain in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: the word for fine weather goes around the other letters

parts.note: fine weather is dry
E is the compass abbreviation for east
R is the weather-map abbreviation for rain

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: fine in the east, rain over Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Reads as a weather forecast; the definition is a place found in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This city, also called Londonderry, lies in the north-west of the province.

clue.text: Never to be tailed back and that's flat!

indicators.note: the shortened word is read backwards
a word tailed has its last letter cut

explanation.surface: A defiant refusal: never to retreat, and that's final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be tailed' cuts NEVER to NEVE; 'back' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Level or smooth ground is described as having no bumps.

clue.text: One fellow doubled back to get her

indicators.note: the doubled letters are read backwards
the two pieces are written twice

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A man retraces his steps twice to win a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'together' is 'to get her' run together; IF doubled is IFIF, turned back by 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a girl's name, so it can stand for a 'her'.

clue.text: Incur, in the preparatory period

definitions.meaning: to ... debts is to incur them
the build-up time before an event

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to accumulate a bill and also the lead-up before something happens.

clue.text: Send out again and again to get the children

parts.note: re is a prefix meaning again
issue means offspring

explanation.surface: Sending something out repeatedly in order to get the kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'again' belongs to the definition; the second gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To republish or put out once more is to send out a second time.

clue.text: Get back and rope off the exterior of the ward

indicators.note: the scrambled rope forms the outside, enclosing the other piece
rope that has come off is in disarray, so the letters are jumbled
in a down clue the word get is read back, upwards

explanation.surface: Retreat and cordon off the outside of the hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ward' tempts as a hospital room; it is the person under guardianship. 'off' gives PROE, 'back' gives TEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A person under a patron's care or guardianship is a ward.

clue.text: The chirping of the mocking bird?

definitions.meaning: the ... sound birds make
one who twits, that is taunts or mocks

explanation.definitionFit: The word is birdsong chatter and, cryptically, someone who twits or teases.

clue.text: Before it he was introduced, if you please!

indicators.note: the two small words are introduced inside the other piece

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: Someone said please before he was presented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' gives the prefix PRE, which is split open; the answer is an old-fashioned word for please.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word, short for 'I pray thee', means please.

clue.text: Tease and upset about the classes

indicators.note: one piece sits about, around, the other

parts.note: read as set put up, the word set backwards in a down clue
to rib someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Teasing and upsetting the people in class.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' can be read as set put up, giving TES; that wraps the word for tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribes are groups or classes of people sharing a lineage.

clue.text: The toast makes one feel better

definitions.meaning: a drinking salute
lifts one's spirits

explanation.surface: A drinking toast that lifts everyone's mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is said when raising glasses and also means it gladdens or encourages.

clue.text: Shut up! There's housework to get on with

definitions.meaning: to confine

definitions.text: There's housework to get on with
definitions.meaning: a cooperative, where household tasks are shared and members get along

explanation.surface: Someone is told to be quiet because there are chores to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to confine as in a hen pen, and also a cooperative.

clue.text: He, time after time, holes out

indicators.note: the holes go on the outside of the other letters

parts.note: a hole looks like O, so two holes give two Os

indicators.note: one time follows the other

parts.note: T again for time
T again for time

explanation.surface: A golfer, time after time, holes his putts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holes out' looks like golf; the two Os sit outside TT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a man's name, so a 'he'.

clue.text: What the rain-washed pavement had?

parts.note: the pavement was bathed by a shower of rain

explanation.surface: A question about a wet pavement.
explanation.walkthrough: The rain shower literally gave the pavement a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bath taken under a spray of water, as the pavement got from the rain.

clue.text: Earned as a return from a dairy import

indicators.note: a return here is a reading backwards

parts.note: made, as in made money

explanation.surface: Profit earned from cheese brought in from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' suggests profit; it signals reading MADE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This Dutch cheese is a dairy product imported to Britain.

clue.text: Look for feeling in the performance

definitions.meaning: a facial look
emotion put into playing music or acting

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a facial look and also expressive feeling in performance.
